title: Testing extension logic with node:test
when: A browser extension has growing logic such as URL matching, settings migration or message handlers, and the user wants fast tests that run without opening a browser.
prompt:
Goal: Pure logic modules free of the global chrome object, tested with node:test and small fakes, plus a manifest guard test.
Steps:
1. Move logic into lib/*.js ES modules: matchSite(url, rules), migrate(old), and handlers that receive dependencies (handleSave(payload, { storage })).
2. Only thin glue files (background.js, popup.js) call chrome.*; they pass chrome.storage.local into lib functions.
3. test/fake-storage.js: an in memory store with async get(defaults), set(obj), remove(keys) and change listeners, returning the same shapes as the real API.
4. test/logic.test.mjs imports test from node:test and assert from node:assert/strict; per handler test a valid payload, missing fields, an unknown type and a rejecting fake.
5. Migration tests: an old schemaVersion object becomes the expected new one, and a second run changes nothing.
6. test/manifest.test.mjs: parse manifest.json, assert manifest_version 3, no "<all_urls>", and every referenced file (worker, icons, pages) exists on disk.
7. package.json "test": "node --test"; no browser or network needed.
Quality bar:
- Tests run in under two seconds.
- lib/ never mentions chrome or window.
Pitfalls:
- A global chrome mock leaking between tests; pass dependencies instead.
- Fakes resolving undefined where the real API returns the defaults object.
Verify:
- [ ] Tests import node:test and node:assert.
- [ ] Manifest test present.
- [ ] lib/ free of chrome calls.
- [ ] node --test passes.
Output: lib/*.js, test/fake-storage.js, test/logic.test.mjs, test/manifest.test.mjs and the test script.

examples.input: testar a logica da minha extensao sem abrir o navegador
examples.output: lib/ modules with injected storage, test/fake-storage.js, logic and migration tests, manifest test checking v3 and files on disk
